name: The Dowse Art Museum
funding: Mostly funded by Hutt City Council, plus the Dowse Foundation; Jan 2025 archive names Dulux as a corporate partner and Steel & Tube as a donor.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Partner page blocked. Live site returns 403. A Jan 2025 Wayback copy names only 'one of' its corporate partners (Dulux), so the full roster is unread.
records_note: A council museum: its Foundation site names supporters and trustees but posts no reports. The museum and council sites were blocked.

name: Sarjeant Gallery
funding: Whanganui District Council ($26.1M) led the NZ$79.4M rebuild with the Ministry for Culture and Heritage, Lottery Grants Board, Provincial Growth Fund, Stout Trust and other unnamed trusts.
watch: Nearly NZ$11M came from community and private trusts and individuals, mostly unnamed. No Lion Foundation, Pub Charity, NZCT or SkyCity is named.
records_note: Parent Whanganui District Council posts audited annual reports 2017 to 2025; the gallery's partners page names funders and its Trust page names nine trustees.

name: Lahore Biennale Foundation
funding: Punjab and federal government bodies; lead sponsor Habib Bank; star sponsors Barjeel Art Foundation, Bareeze and ICCI; partners include Nishat, PIA, Dulux and Careem.
watch: The sponsor page is undated and shows logos only.
records_note: Its Financials page posts reports 2015 to 2025 and statements 2015 to 2024, its Board page lists the board, and sponsors appear as logos.

name: Museo del Barro
funding: Private foundation museum (Escobar, Salerno); 2026 sponsors page names Banco Itaú, Citibank, French embassy, a law firm and named friends.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Sponsors page under construction. Bank money named: Itaú (sponsor) and Citibank (supporter).
records_note: Its sponsors page names a bank sponsor, supporters and named friends, but the site posts no annual reports, accounts or foundation board.

name: MAC Lima
funding: Private museum in Barranco; sponsors include Fundación Telefónica, Fundación BBVA, Credicorp, UTEC, EU delegation, Getty Foundation, Bloomberg.
watch: Supporter roster unverified. Bloomberg is listed as a sponsor. It is under active campaign elsewhere; the atlas lists Bloomberg-roster institutions as B. No protest found at MAC Lima.
records_note: Its Auspicios page shows ten sponsor logos with no date; the site posts no annual reports, accounts or board, and no Peruvian register was found.

name: Ateneo Art Gallery
funding: University museum of Ateneo de Manila University, founded 1960 on Fernando Zobel's gift of his collection; later donors, including artists, added works.
records_note: Ateneo's pages all returned 403, so its reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; only Wikipedia was readable.

name: Metropolitan Museum of Manila
funding: Formerly central-bank subsidised; now a non-profit foundation (1979, Imelda Marcos, Bienvenido Tantoco Sr.). Founding benefactors include Campos family firms NutriAsia and Del Monte Philippines; Metrobank and NCCA back programmes.
watch: NutriAsia, named a benefactor in 2021, saw police break up its 2018 Marilao strike: at least 30 people injured, 19 arrested.
records_note: Its site describes a non-government, not-for-profit foundation and posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; no Philippine register was readable.

name: Museo de Arte de Ponce
funding: Founders Ferré-Rangel and Fonalledas families and Fundación Ángel Ramos; 700+ individuals; corporate gala sponsors led by Banco Popular.
watch: Supporter roster unverified. Fossil money on its own sponsors page: Puma Energy, New Fortress Energy, plus UBS. The list is from the 2019 gala. The site also carries injected casino spam.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2022-23 and 2023-24 and a named sponsor list with 2019 gala tiers; no accounts on its site, but the operating foundation's Form 990 is public.

name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Puerto Rico
funding: Non-profit (EIN 66-0420190); 2026 funders: NEA, IMLS, Luce, Wallace, Teiger, Banco Popular, Walmart, PR Tourism Co., The Macallan.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Site returned no content. Moved to museomac.org. Names alcohol (The Macallan), retail (Walmart) and bank (Banco Popular) money. No controversy found.
records_note: Form 990 filings for 2020 to 2024 are on ProPublica; its sponsorship page shows three undated logos, and its board and team pages return 404.

name: Dak'Art Biennale
funding: Financed by the Senegalese state through the culture ministry; its sponsors page names the Prime Minister's office, City of Dakar, UNESCO, ECOWAS, Ecobank, SUNU Group and Sococim (cement).
watch: The 16th edition runs 19 November to 19 December 2026.
records_note: It shows sponsor logos without names or dates and names its 20-member steering committee, but posts no annual reports or accounts.

name: Musée des Civilisations Noires
funding: Senegalese state museum. China financed the building with a CFA 20 billion (over EUR 30M) grant. 2025 own revenue was CFA 353.9M.
watch: China's grant paid for the building, not operations.
records_note: Its site did not open from here; a search listing shows a 2025 activity report, and nothing on accounts, funders or board was checked.

name: STPI Creative Workshop & Gallery
funding: Non-profit founded 2002; National Arts Council support plus patrons (S$2,500 individual, S$5,000 corporate) targeting S$300k.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Patron and corporate partner list not retrievable. Support page lists tiers only, no named patrons; annual report not online; Wayback rate-limited (429). No controversy found.
records_note: Its About page names ten board members; it posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list, and the governance page is one paragraph.
